AppleAuthorizationRequestCustomizer
Customizes the authorization request: Apple only hands over the name and the e-mail address of the user when the response is posted to the redirect URI (response_mode=form_post), so the request made for Apple's client id asks for it.
AppleClientSecretGenerator
Generates the client secret Sign in with Apple requires: a JWT signed with ES256 by the key Apple issued (iss the team id, sub the client id, aud https://appleid.apple.com, header kid the key id), valid for a short time.
ApplePrivateKeyParser
Reads the private key Apple issues for Sign in with Apple (an EC P-256 key in PKCS#8 PEM form, the content of the .p8 file) from the text an environment variable holds, where line breaks are often written as a literal \n.
AppleProviderCondition
Condition that holds when Sign in with Apple is configured, so the key of its client secret is only parsed and its special handling (the signed client secret, the form post callback) only installed then.
AppleTokenRequestCustomizer
Customizes the parameters of the token request of the authorization code grant: the request made for Apple's client id carries the signed JWT of AppleClientSecretGenerator as its client_secret, in place of the empty secret the registration holds.
AsyncConfiguration
Enables @Async methods for every feature of the application (the delivery of one-time tokens after their transaction commits, ...), which then run on Spring Boot's applicationTaskExecutor.
AudienceRolesOpaqueTokenIntrospector
Decorates an introspector of the opaque-token variant: rejects tokens whose audience is not accepted and adds the role authorities of the roles attribute, so the opaque variant behaves like the JWT one.

FederatedOAuth2UserService
The user service of the providers that are plain OAuth 2.0 (GitHub), which have no ID token: the framework's service reads the profile from the provider's API, the verified primary e-mail address is read from /user/emails (through the domain port VerifiedEmailLookup, implemented by the GitHub adapter of infrastructure/github with a client generated from the contract of that GitHub operation), the account is resolved (found, linked by verified e-mail or provisioned, and refused when it may not sign in) and the principal becomes the local one, named after the account.
FederatedOidcUserService
The user service of the OpenID Connect providers (Google, Microsoft, Apple): the framework's service loads the user as it always does (the ID token, and the UserInfo endpoint where the provider has one), then the account is resolved (found, linked by verified e-mail or provisioned, and refused when it may not sign in) and the principal becomes the local one, named after the account.
FederatedUserMapper
Maps the user an external provider described onto the user the rest of the server sees: the principal of the session, whose name is the local account's username (so it is the sub of the issued tokens, as it is for every other way of signing in), whose authorities are the account's own, and which still carries the claims of the provider (the amr among them).

Thrown when the value sent to bind a certificate is not a single PEM X.509 certificate within its validity period.
InvalidClientJwksException
Raised when the public JWK set of a client is not a valid JWK set, is empty or holds a key with private material.
InvalidCredentialsException
The username or the current password is wrong.
InvalidPasskeyLabelException
Thrown when the label given to a passkey is refused: blank, or longer than allowed once trimmed.
InvalidPasswordException
The chosen password breaks the PasswordPolicy.
InvalidPhoneCodeException
The verification code of a phone number is wrong, has expired or there is no verification in progress.
InvalidPhoneNumberException
Thrown when the text typed as a phone number is not a valid number.
InvalidTotpCodeException
Thrown when the code presented to confirm the enrolment of an authenticator app is wrong.
IsClientMfaRequiredUseCase
Use case that tells whether a client makes multi-factor authentication mandatory for every user signing in through it (ClientRegistration.mfaRequired()).
IssuedTokenClaims
The claims this server adds to the tokens it issues, whatever their format, so the self-contained (JWT) access tokens and the reference (opaque) ones carry the same claims: RolesTenantAudienceTokenCustomizer applies it to the JWTs and ReferenceTokenClaimsCustomizer to the claims stored for a reference token (which the introspection endpoint returns).
IsTotpEnabledUseCase
Use case that tells whether a user has a confirmed authenticator app.
IsUserMfaRequiredUseCase
Use case that tells whether the account of a user requires a second factor, whatever the client being served: when an administrator forced it (users.mfa_required) or when the user has confirmed a second factor (asked to HasConfirmedSecondFactorUseCase), since a factor the user enrolled must protect every sign-in.
JavaTimeFormatter
Class that add parsing/formatting support for Java 8+ OffsetDateTime class.
JavaTimeFormatter
Class that add parsing/formatting support for Java 8+ OffsetDateTime class.
JavaTimeFormatter
Class that add parsing/formatting support for Java 8+ OffsetDateTime class.
JdbcAccountTokenRepository
AccountTokenRepository over the account_tokens table.
JdbcAuthorizationServerConfiguration
Registers the JDBC implementations of the Spring Authorization Server persistence services.
JdbcCertificateBindingRepository
CertificateBindingRepository over the x509_certificates table.
JdbcClientAssertionReplayRegistry
ClientAssertionReplayRegistry over the client_assertion_jtis table.
JdbcClientRegistrationRepository
ClientRegistrationRepository over Spring Authorization Server's RegisteredClientRepository (the JDBC one), which reads and writes the oauth2_registered_client table.
JdbcExpiredLinkTokenPurger
ExpiredLinkTokenPurger over Spring Security's one_time_tokens table (magic links).
JdbcFederatedIdentityRepository
FederatedIdentityRepository over the federated_identities table.
JdbcGeneratedPasswordRepository
GeneratedPasswordRepository over the generated column of user_passwords.
JdbcOneTimeCodeRepository
OneTimeCodeRepository over the ott_codes table.
JdbcPasskeyRepository
PasskeyRepository over the user_credentials and user_entities tables that Spring Security's WebAuthn repositories own.
JdbcPhoneVerificationRepository
PhoneVerificationRepository over the pending_* columns of the user_phones table.
JdbcRecoveryCodeRepository
RecoveryCodeRepository over the recovery_codes table.
JdbcSecondFactorAttemptRepository
SecondFactorAttemptRepository over the second_factor_attempts table.
JdbcSecurityEventRepository
SecurityEventRepository over the security_events table.
JdbcSigningKeyRepository
SigningKeyRepository over the signing_keys table.
JdbcSignInMethodsLock
SignInMethodsLock over a PostgreSQL transaction-level advisory lock on the account: it opens no transaction and holds the lock until the caller's ends, so the removals of the sign-in methods of one account (unlinking an identity, unbinding a certificate) run one after the other and each counts what the previous one left.
JdbcSmsCostLedgerRepository
SmsCostLedgerRepository over the sms_cost_ledger table.
JdbcTimestamps
Converts between the domain's Instant and the OffsetDateTime the PostgreSQL driver binds to and reads from a timestamp with time zone column.
JdbcTotpCredentialRepository
TotpCredentialRepository over the totp_credentials table.
JdbcTrustedDeviceRepository
TrustedDeviceRepository over the trusted_devices table.
JdbcUserAccountRepository
UserAccountRepository reading user accounts from the users, user_authorities and user_passwords tables.
JdbcUserAuthorizationRepository
UserAuthorizationRepository over the oauth2_authorization table.
JdbcUserMfaSettingsRepository
UserMfaSettingsRepository over the mfa_required column of the users table.
JdbcUserPhoneRepository
UserPhoneRepository over the verified columns of the user_phones table.
JwkCacheRefreshListener
Drops every cached JWK set when the signing keys rotate, so the next token or JWKS request sees the new keys without waiting for the cache to expire.
JwtClaimsContributor
Extension point that lets a feature add claims to the tokens issued by the authorization server: the access tokens, whether self-contained (JWT) or reference (their claims are returned by the introspection endpoint), and the ID tokens.
KeyEncryptionConfiguration
Reads the key-encryption inputs from configuration (authserver.keys.encryption.password and authserver.keys.encryption.salt, taken from the environment in production).
KeyEncryptionProperties
Inputs of the encryption of private signing keys at rest.
KeyEncryptionTestConfiguration
Supplies the inputs of the encryption of signing keys at rest to a test context.
Keytool
Runs the keytool of the JDK that runs the tests and cleans up the temporary directories its key stores live in; the JDK has no public API to issue a certificate.
LastSignInMethodException
Thrown when removing a sign-in method would leave the account with none, so its owner could never sign in again.
LegacyImplicitAccessTokenToken
The result of a granted legacy implicit request: the access token and what the response needs to send it to the client in the fragment of its redirect URI.
LegacyImplicitAuthenticationProvider
Grants the legacy implicit request: after checking the client, its redirect URI, the user, the multi-factor policy, the state and the scopes, it issues an access token (never a refresh token) through the token generator, stores the authorization (so the token can be introspected and revoked) and returns it for the response handler.
LegacyImplicitAuthorizationRequestConverter
Reads an authorization request with response_type=token.
LegacyImplicitAuthorizationRequestToken
An authorization request of the legacy implicit flow (response_type=token), not yet authenticated: the request as the client sent it and the user the request arrived with.
LegacyImplicitClientSeeder
Registers the one client of the legacy implicit flow at start-up, when it does not exist yet: public, grant implicit only (no refresh token, no consent), one redirect URI, a restricted scope and audience and the lifetime of the flow.
LegacyImplicitConfiguration
Enables the legacy implicit flow.
LegacyImplicitErrorToken
The result of a legacy implicit request that was refused after its redirect URI had been checked, so the refusal is sent to the client in the fragment of the redirect URI.
LegacyImplicitProperties
Settings of the legacy implicit flow, bound from authserver.legacy-implicit.* (see application-legacy-implicit.yml).
LegacyImplicitProtocolChainCustomizer
Adds the legacy implicit flow to the authorization endpoint: its converter first, its provider first and its response handler in place of the framework's (which it delegates to for an authorization code).
LegacyImplicitResponseHandler
Answers the authorization endpoint: for the two results of the legacy implicit flow it redirects with 302 to the registered redirect URI and carries the token, or the error, in its fragment (so it never reaches a server log as a query would); any other result is the framework's authorization code response and goes to the delegate.
LegacyImplicitTokenGeneratorFactory
Builds the token generator of the legacy flow with the claims customizers of the server, so its tokens carry the same roles, tenant, audience and authentication claims as those of the other flows.
LibPhoneNumberCountryResolver
PhoneCountryResolver over libphonenumber: the region of an E.164 number.
LibPhoneNumberNormalizer
PhoneNormalizer backed by Google libphonenumber: accepts only valid numbers and never throws.
LinkIdentityUseCase
Use case that links an identity of an external provider to the account of a signed-in user.
LinkTokenUsername
The user name a magic link token is stored with.
ListCertificatesUseCase
Use case that lists the client certificates bound to an account.
ListClientsUseCase
Use case that lists every registered client.
ListDocumentsOnBehalfOfUseCase
Use case that lists the documents a user may see, on behalf of that user (token exchange).
ListDocumentsUseCase
Use case that lists the documents of the signed-in user.
ListDocumentsUseCase
Use case that lists documents: those of one owner, or all of them.
ListDocumentsUseCase
Use case that lists the documents the service client may see with its own (client credentials) token.
ListIdentitiesUseCase
Use case that lists the identities of external providers linked to an account.
ListPasskeysUseCase
Use case that lists the passkeys of a user.
ListSigningKeysUseCase
Use case that lists every stored signing key, whatever its state, for administration.
ListTrustedDevicesUseCase
Use case that lists the trusted devices of a user that have not expired.
LockSignInMethodsUseCase
Use case that locks the sign-in methods of an account for the rest of the caller's transaction and counts them: a password its owner knows (not a generated one), the linked identities, a passkey and the bound certificates.
LoggingSmsSender
Default SmsSender: sends nothing, it records the message in the SmsOutbox and logs the masked recipient.
LoginApi
 
LoginChainCustomizer
Extension point that lets an authentication method customize the login/UI security filter chain.
LoginContentSecurityPolicy
Builds the content security policy of the server-rendered pages from the BrandingProperties: same-origin resources only and no framing, except that images may also be data: URIs (the QR code of an authenticator app, rendered in memory so its secret never becomes a resource of its own) and, when the branding logo is an absolute http(s) URL, come from its origin (img-src 'self' data: <scheme://host[:port]>).
LoginController
Serves the login page, as the contract apis/auth-server/web-pages/auth-server-pages-v1.yaml describes it through the generated LoginPageApi, supplying the ordered login method fragments and the outcome of the last attempt to the template.
LoginErrorMessages
Maps the exception of a failed sign-in, which Spring Security keeps in the SPRING_SECURITY_LAST_EXCEPTION session attribute, to the key of the message the login page shows.
LoginHeadersCustomizer
Adds the security headers of the server-rendered pages: the content security policy that LoginContentSecurityPolicy builds (same-origin resources only, no framing, and the origin of an absolute branding logo URL for images), X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy.
LoginMethodFragment
Extension point that lets an authentication method contribute a Thymeleaf fragment to the login page.
LoginPageApi
 
LoginStaticResourcesCustomizer
Permits the stylesheet shared by the server-rendered pages, which must load before anybody has signed in.
LogoutChainCustomizer
Configures how a user signs out of the login/UI chain: a POST to "/logout" (protected by CSRF, so a third-party page cannot sign the user out) invalidates the session, deletes its cookie and returns to the login page.
LogoutConfiguration
Wires the OpenID Connect RP-initiated logout of the BFF.
LogoutController
Serves the page that asks the user to confirm signing out, as the contract apis/auth-server/web-pages/auth-server-pages-v1.yaml describes it through the generated LogoutPageApi.
LogoutPageApi
 
MailConfiguration
Wires the SMTP implementation of AccountMailer.
Mailpit
Describes the Mailpit container the one-time token tests read the e-mail of: the pinned image, its two ports and a factory that builds the container and the client of its HTTP API.
MailpitClient
Reads the messages a Mailpit server received through its HTTP API, so a test finds the code or the link the application mailed to a recipient.
MailpitClient.Message
A message Mailpit received.
MailpitTestConfiguration
Starts a Mailpit container for a Spring test context and points the application's mail sender at it, so the messages the application sends can be read back through MailpitClient.
MailProperties
Settings of the e-mails sent by SmtpAccountMailer.
MfaAuthorizationManager
Decides whether an authentication has presented enough factors for the request being served: when the client or the user requires multi-factor authentication, the factors must satisfy the MfaPolicy; otherwise any authentication does.
MfaClaimsContributor
Adds to the access and ID tokens how the user authenticated: amr (the RFC 8176 values of the factors really presented, plus mfa when there are at least two), acr (the class of the authentication, see AuthenticationContextClass) and auth_time (the epoch second the primary factor was presented, a number per OIDC; access tokens only, because the framework sets it on ID tokens).
MfaConfiguration
Wires multi-factor authentication: Spring Security's multi-factor support (it enables the entry points for a missing factor authority; the factors are not required globally, because the MfaAuthorizationManager requires them only when the client or the user asks for it), the registry of AuthenticationFactor beans, the policy manager, and its application to the login chain and to /oauth2/authorize.
MfaConfiguration
Exposes the domain collaborators of the multi-factor use cases as beans, so no use case creates them and a deployment (or a test) can replace any of them, and binds the MfaProperties.
MfaExceptionHandler
Translates the failures of the authenticator app, recovery code and trusted device endpoints to RFC 9457 problem details, answered as application/problem+json.
MfaLoginChainCustomizer
Applies the multi-factor policy to the login/UI chain: the consent page needs the factors the policy asks for, and a user who lacks a registered second factor is sent to the second-factor page instead of getting a 403.
MfaPolicy
The rule that decides when the factors of an authentication are enough, and when they are required.
MfaProperties
Multi-factor settings, bound once from authserver.mfa.* and injected wherever one of them is needed (the use cases of this module and the step-up guard of the API).
MfaProtocolChainCustomizer
Applies the multi-factor policy to /oauth2/authorize: a user whose client or account requires a second factor and has not presented one is sent to the second-factor page, with the authorize request saved, before any code is issued.
MissingSmsGatewayConfiguration
Stops the startup when no SMS gateway is configured: none of the profiles that provide an SmsSender (twilio, sns, or dev / test for the logging one) is active.
MtlsEndpointAliases
Builds the mtls_endpoint_aliases metadata claim of RFC 8705 (section 5): the addresses of the endpoints that authenticate clients on the dedicated TLS port, the issuer's host with authserver.x509.port.
MtlsProperties
Configuration of the mutual-TLS client authentication (authserver.mtls.*, RFC 8705).
MtlsTrustAnchors
The certificate authorities trusted for tls_client_auth, loaded once at startup.
NimbusSignedTokenService
Issues and verifies purpose-bound tokens as JWTs signed with the active signing key and verified against the published keys.
OAuth2ClientConfiguration
The OAuth2 client of the service client: its registrations, the authorized client manager that caches the access tokens and renews them shortly before they expire, and the documents client that sends them.
OnBehalfOfDocumentGateway
Port to the documents on the resource server, read on behalf of a user: the subject token of the user is exchanged for a token for the resource server (RFC 8693).
OnBehalfOfDocumentsApis
Builds the documents client of a user: its requests carry the access token that the authorization server issues in exchange for the user's own token.
OneTimeCode
A numeric one-time code that was issued to a user.
OneTimeCodeGenerator
Port that generates the numeric codes users type.
OneTimeCodeHasher
Port that hashes one-time codes so that only the hash is stored.
OneTimeCodeRepository
Port that stores the numeric one-time codes.
OneTimeCodeRequestResult
Outcome of a request for a one-time code.
OneTimeCodeRowMapper
Maps a row of the ott_codes table to a OneTimeCode.
OneTimeTokenPageApi
 
OneTimeTokenServiceConfiguration
Registers Spring Security's JDBC one-time token service, which stores the magic link tokens in the one_time_tokens table instead of in memory.
OpenApiConfig
Runtime OpenAPI documents of the authorization server, served by springdoc.
OpenApiConfig
Runtime OpenAPI document of the JSON API of the BFF, served by springdoc at "/v3/api-docs" to a signed-in user.
OpenApiConfig
Runtime OpenAPI document of the HTTP API of the resource server, served by springdoc at "/v3/api-docs".
OpenApiContract
Compares an OpenAPI contract under apis/ with the OpenAPI document a running application serves.
OttAuthenticationConverter
Reads what is posted to POST /login/ott: the token field holds either the token of a magic link (a UUID, which OttLinkAuthenticationProvider consumes) or the numeric code of an e-mail or SMS, which is tied to the identifier and the binding id the session of the browser holds.
OttAuthenticationFailureHandler
Sends the browser back after a failed submission to POST /login/ott: a wrong numeric code goes to the page where it is typed (/login/ott?error), so the user can try again, and a magic link that is not valid goes to the sign-in page (/login?error).
OttAuthenticationSuccessHandler
Forgets the pending token of the session once it was used, then lets the delegate resume the request the sign-in interrupted.
OttChainCustomizer
Adds the one-time token methods to the login/UI chain through http.oneTimeTokenLogin(...): the request of a token (POST /ott/generate), the submission of a magic link token or a numeric code (POST /login/ott) and, as a second factor, the submission of a code (POST /login/second-factor/ott).
OttChainCustomizer.SessionStrategyConfigurer
Hands the session authentication strategy of the chain to the second-factor filter.
OttChannel
Channel through which a one-time token reaches the user.
OttCleanupJob
Scheduled entry point that deletes what one-time tokens leave behind once it expired: the numeric codes, the pending phone verifications, the SMS cost ledger entries past their retention and Spring's expired link tokens.
OttCleanupResult
Number of rows removed by a cleanup run.
OttCodeAuthenticationProvider
Signs a user in with a numeric one-time code, delivered by e-mail or SMS, through VerifyOneTimeCodeUseCase.
OttCodeAuthenticationToken
Request to sign in with a numeric one-time code: the code the user typed, the identifier it was requested for and the binding id of the session that requested it.
OttConfiguration
Wires the one-time token methods into the login/UI chain.
OttConfiguration
Declares the collaborators of the one-time-code use cases as beans, so they can be replaced and mocked.
OttDelivery
Port that delivers a one-time token to a destination through a channel.
OttDeliveryException
Thrown when a one-time token could not be delivered.
OttDeliveryListener
Delivers the one-time tokens the use cases asked for, once the transaction that stored them has committed (TransactionPhase.AFTER_COMMIT; an event published outside a transaction is delivered at once) and off the request thread (@Async, on Spring Boot's applicationTaskExecutor).
OttDestination
Where a one-time code of a user is delivered.
OttExceptionHandler
Translates the failures of the phone endpoints to RFC 9457 problem details, answered as application/problem+json.
OttFactors
Registers the one-time token methods as authentication factors.
OttGenerateRequestResolver
Resolves the request of POST /ott/generate to the token Spring's filter asks the token service for.
OttGenerationParameters
What a request to POST /ott/generate asks for, read from its form fields: through which channel, a numeric code or a magic link, and for a sign-in or as a second factor.
OttGenerationSuccessHandler
Delivers the token Spring's filter just generated, and answers every request the same way.
OttKind
Shape of a one-time token.
OttLinkAuthenticationProvider
Confirms a magic link: consumes the token Spring's JdbcOneTimeTokenService stored and signs the user in with it.
OttLinkFactory
Builds the magic link of a token.
OttLoginMethodFragment
Contributes the one-time token sign-in to the login page: a form that asks for the identifier and whether to receive a code or a magic link by e-mail, or a code by SMS, and posts it to POST /ott/generate.
OttPagesController
Serves the two pages of the one-time token flow, as the contract apis/auth-server/web-pages/ auth-server-pages-v1.yaml describes them through the generated OneTimeTokenPageApi: the page where the code is entered (or that says to check the inbox when a magic link was requested) and the page a magic link opens, whose button posts the token.
OttPolicy
The rules of one-time tokens: how long each kind lives, how long a code is and how many wrong submissions are tolerated.
OttProperties
Settings of the one-time codes, bound from authserver.ott.* once and validated at startup.
OttProviders
The authentication providers of the one-time token methods, held together.
OttPurpose
What a one-time token is used for.
OttRateLimiter
Rate limiter of the one-time token endpoints, on the pattern of the account endpoints' limiter: Bucket4j token buckets in Caffeine caches (FixedWindowBuckets).
OttRateLimitExceededException
A client address or an identifier requested or submitted more one-time tokens than its window allows.
OttRateLimitFilter
Applies OttRateLimiter to the one-time token endpoints, which are Spring Security filters (so no controller advice sees their failures): POST /ott/generate counts as a token request and POST /login/ott and POST /login/second-factor/ott as submissions, each per client address and per identifier.
OttRateLimitProperties
Configuration of the rate limiting of the one-time token endpoints (authserver.ott.rate-limit.*): the requests for a token (POST /ott/generate, the phone enrolment) and the submissions of a token or a code (POST /login/ott, POST /login/second-factor/ott, the phone verification).
OttSecondFactorAuthenticationProvider
Verifies a numeric one-time code, delivered by e-mail or SMS, as the second factor of the signed-in user through VerifyOneTimeCodeUseCase, which counts the failures against the second-factor lockout, locks after too many, clears the counter on success and records the security events: a locked second factor is rejected even for a correct code.
OttSecondFactorChannels
Decides through which channels a one-time code or link may be the second factor of a signed-in user.
OttSecondFactorFilter
Processes the post of the one-time code form of the second factor (POST /login/second-factor/ott), in the way TotpAuthenticationFilter processes the TOTP forms.
OttSecondFactorFragment
Contributes the one-time token second factor to the second-factor page: the buttons that send a code or a magic link by e-mail and a code by SMS to the signed-in user, each posting to POST /ott/generate with the second-factor purpose.
OttSecondFactorToken
Request to verify a one-time code as a second factor: the authentication the user already holds (the primary factor), the code the user typed and the binding id of the session that requested it.
OttVerificationResult
Outcome of the verification of a one-time code.
OttVerificationResult.Status
What happened when a code was verified.
PageRenderer
Renders a server-rendered page (a Thymeleaf template) to the text/html answer of an operation generated from the pages contract.
ParConfiguration
Enables pushed authorization requests (RFC 9126) when authserver.par.enabled is true: a client authenticates at POST /oauth2/par, receives a one-time request_uri and then sends the user to the authorization endpoint with it.
Passkey
A WebAuthn credential registered by the account
Passkey
A passkey (WebAuthn credential) registered by a user.
PasskeyChainCustomizer
Customizes the login/UI chain with the passkeys (WebAuthn).
PasskeyConfiguration
Installs the passkeys (WebAuthn) in the login/UI chain.
PasskeyConfiguration
Binds the PasskeyProperties.
PasskeyController
Manages the passkeys of the authenticated account (the operations of the contract).
PasskeyDtoMapper
Maps the passkeys of the domain onto the DTO generated from the contract.
PasskeyExceptionHandler
Answers the failures of the passkeys API as application/problem+json.
PasskeyFactor
Registers a passkey (WebAuthn credential) as an authentication factor: a strong primary one, because the authenticator proves possession of the key and, with user verification, the user as well, so it satisfies the multi-factor policy on its own.
PasskeyLoginMethodFragment
Contributes the passkey sign-in to the login page: a button and a field the browser fills with the passkeys it knows (conditional mediation).
PasskeyNotFoundException
Thrown when a user has no passkey with the requested identifier.
PasskeyProperties
Relying party settings of the passkeys (WebAuthn), bound once from authserver.passkeys.* and injected wherever one of them is needed.
PasskeyRegistrationAuthorizationManager
Lets a request to the registration endpoints of the WebAuthn filters (/webauthn/register and everything below it) through only when the session satisfies the multi-factor policy of its account.
PasskeyRegistrationFilter
The authorization filter that guards the registration endpoints of the WebAuthn filters.
PasskeyRepository
Port that reads and manages the passkeys users registered.
PasskeyRowMapper
Maps a row of the user_credentials table to a Passkey.
PasskeysApi
 
PasskeySecondFactorFragment
Contributes the "use a passkey" action to the second-factor page.
PasskeySecondFactorLockoutFilter
Applies the second-factor lockout to a passkey that completes a second-factor step.
PasskeysPageApi
 
PasskeysPageController
Renders the account page where the signed-in user registers passkeys.
PasskeyView
What the passkeys page shows of a passkey.
PasskeyViewMapper
Maps the passkeys of the domain onto the view model of the passkeys page.
PasswordAuthenticationConfiguration
Declares the authentication provider of the password-based sign-in, instead of the one Spring Security builds from the UserDetailsService bean, to close a user enumeration.
PasswordConfiguration
Registers the password encoder of the password-based sign-in and of the client secrets: new values are encoded with Argon2, while bcrypt and PBKDF2 hashes stay verifiable (and are upgraded on the next successful sign-in).
PasswordFactor
Registers the password as an authentication factor: a primary one, which needs a second factor to satisfy the policy.
PasswordHasher
Port that hashes and checks passwords.
PasswordLoginFragment
Contributes the username and password form to the login page, as every authentication method does through the LoginMethodFragment extension point.
PasswordPolicy
Password rules in the style of NIST SP 800-63B: a minimum and a maximum length, no composition rules (no required digits, symbols or upper-case letters) and a password that does not contain the username.
PasswordPolicyConfiguration
Exposes the domain's PasswordPolicy as a bean, so the use cases that check a new password depend on the policy instead of creating it, and a deployment can replace it with a policy of its own.
PasswordResetRequest
Request of a password reset link
PasswordViolation
A rule of the PasswordPolicy that a candidate password breaks.
PemCertificateReader
Reads the certificate sent to bind it to an account: exactly one X.509 certificate in PEM form, within its validity period, with a subject.
PendingIdentityLink
The marker a signed-in user leaves in the session when asking to link an identity of an external provider: the next sign-in with that provider, before the marker expires, links the identity to this account instead of signing anybody in.
PendingIdentityLinks
Keeps the link marker (PendingIdentityLink) of the explicit link flow: the identities page records it in the session before sending the browser to the provider, and the user services consume it when the provider sends the user back.
PendingOtt
The one-time token a browser has asked for and not used yet, kept in its session: for whom, through which channel, of which kind and for what purpose, and the binding id the numeric code was stored with.
PendingRecoveryCodes
Keeps, in the session, the recovery codes generated when an authenticator app is enrolled during the sign-in, from the post that confirms it until the page that shows them once (RecoveryCodesPageController), which takes them out of the session.
PhoneApi
 
PhoneController
Shows, enrols, verifies and removes the phone number of the authenticated account, the number the SMS codes go to.
PhoneCountryResolver
Port that tells the country of a phone number.
PhoneDtoMapper
Maps the results of the phone use cases onto the DTOs generated from the contract.
PhoneEnrolmentResponse
Confirmation that a verification code was requested
PhoneEnrolmentStarted
Outcome of starting a phone enrolment.
PhoneNormalizer
Port that turns the phone number a user typed into E.164.
PhoneNotFoundException
The account has no verified phone number.
PhoneNumber
A phone number in E.164 format.
PhonePageApi
 
PhonePageChainCustomizer
Keeps the phone page and its form posts behind the multi-factor policy, as the passkeys page is: a session that only presented the password of an account that still has to complete its second factor is sent to the second-factor page instead of being able to change the phone that receives the codes.
PhonePageController
Serves the phone account page and the session-protected form posts it uses, as the contract apis/auth-server/web-pages/auth-server-pages-v1.yaml describes them through the generated PhonePageApi.
PhoneResponse
The verified phone number of the account
PhoneSessionStepUp
The step-up rule of StepUpGuard for a browser session instead of a bearer token: while the account has a confirmed second factor, a sensitive change (removing the phone) needs a session that shows a multi-factor sign-in made within authserver.mfa.step-up-max-age; an account without a second factor cannot step up, so it is not asked to.
PhoneVerification
A pending verification of a phone number: the code that was sent to it, hashed, until the user types it.
PhoneVerificationRepository
Port that stores the pending phone verification of each user, with the code hashed.
PhoneVerificationRowMapper
Maps the pending_* columns of a row of the user_phones table to a PhoneVerification.
PollOutcome
What one poll of the token endpoint answered (RFC 8628 section 3.5).
PollOutcome.Failed
Any other error (access_denied, expired_token, ...): the flow is over.
PollOutcome.Granted
The user approved the request.
PollOutcome.Pending
authorization_pending: the user has not decided yet; poll again after the same interval.
PollOutcome.SlowDown
slow_down: polling too fast; the interval grows by DeviceFlowCli.SLOW_DOWN_INCREMENT_SECONDS.
PostgresIT
Meta-annotation for integration tests backed by a PostgreSQL Testcontainers container.
PostgresTestConfiguration
Exposes a PostgreSQL Testcontainers container as a Spring Boot service connection, so the DataSource (and Flyway) of a test context is wired to it automatically.
Preconditions
Argument checks shared by the domain models.
PresentedCertificate
What a binding keeps of a certificate sent to the account API: its fingerprint, which identifies it, and its subject, which only tells the bindings apart.
PrimaryFactorSession
Rules about the session a one-time token is used as a second factor in: it must already hold a primary factor, and the second factor must not be the very channel that signed the user in (an e-mail code after an e-mail sign-in would prove the same mailbox twice).
PrincipalMapper
Builds the principals the authorized client manager caches tokens under.
PrivateKeyJwkResolver
Resolves the key that signs the private_key_jwt assertion: the unencrypted PKCS#8 PEM RSA private key of ServiceClientKeyProperties, with its public half derived from it and the RS256 algorithm.
Problem
RFC 9457 problem details.
Problem

Adds the sign-in with a client certificate to the login/UI chain through http.x509(...).
X509ChainCustomizer.SessionStrategyConfigurer
Hands the session authentication strategy of the chain to the success handler.
X509Configuration
Installs the sign-in with a client certificate in the login/UI chain, only while authserver.x509.enabled is true.
X509Factor
Registers the client certificate as an authentication factor: a strong primary one, because the holder proves possession of the private key during the TLS handshake (or the proxy did on the server's behalf), so a certificate satisfies the multi-factor policy on its own.
X509ForwardedHeadersGuard
Refuses to start when a certificate may be forwarded in a header while the server rewrites the address of its clients from the forwarded headers.
X509LoginFilter
The X.509 filter of the sign-in path.
X509LoginMethodFragment
Contributes the sign-in with a client certificate to the login page: a form with one button that posts, with the CSRF token, to POST /login/x509.
X509Properties
Configuration of the sign-in with a client certificate (authserver.x509.*).
X509TlsConnectorCustomizer
Adds the dedicated TLS port that requests a client certificate, when authserver.x509.port is set.
X509TlsKeyStore
The key store that holds the server certificate of the dedicated TLS port.
X509TlsKeyStoreResolver
Decides which key store holds the server certificate of the dedicated TLS port: the configured one or, under the dev profile and with none configured, the generated one.
X509UserDetailsService
Loads the account a client certificate is bound to.
